stem:
Uma has a sore throat and fever. Her mother wants to give leftover antibiotic tablets from an earlier illness. The doctor advises against this.

Why should antibiotics be taken only when a doctor prescribes them for a bacterial infection?

options.text: Antibiotics work against every infection, so taking them early always cures the illness faster.
Antibiotics kill bacteria, and careless use can let resistant bacteria develop, making future infections harder to treat.
A fever alone means an antibiotic is needed.
Antibiotics become stronger each time they are used, so frequent use keeps them powerful.

teacher.key_rationale: Antibiotics target bacteria; careless use breeds resistance. Saying they work on every infection omits the bacterial limit. Fever alone captures one symptom as a prescription rule. Saying they get stronger reverses the resistance effect.
